subject: Node inconsistent with parent in Poisson observation model of count data

messages.author: 7790fa9c4dece5fc
messages.subject: Node inconsistent with parent in Poisson observation model of count data
parts:
Hello every, I am hoping I might get some advice on what I suspect to be a rather silly question. I am running an IPM and using a state-space model to analyze the count data. For the observation model I am using a Poisson distribution, which works wonderfully when using deterministic process equations. But when I add in demographic stochasticity I keep getting the "Node inconsistent with parents" error referring to the count data (in the examle below, the specific error is "3 nodes produced errors; first error: Error in node C[21] Node inconsistent with parents")

Population model code:

# Population count data (state-space model)
# Model for the initial stage-specific population sizes

N1  ~ dnorm(2000,0.01)I(0,)
N[1,1] <- round(N1)
N2  ~ dnorm(2000,0.01)I(0,)
N[2,1] <- round(N2)
N3  ~ dnorm(2000,0.01)I(0,)
N[3,1] <- round(N3)
N4 ~ dnorm(8000,0.01)I(0,)
N[4,1] <- round(N4)  



# Process model over time: our model of population dynamics
for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
  N[1,t+1] ~ dpois(N[4,t] * fecund[t] / 2 * alpha[1,t])
  N[2,t+1] ~ dbin(alpha[1,t], N[1,t])
  N[3,t+1] ~ dbin(alpha[1,t], N[2,t])
  N[4,t+1] ~ dbin(alpha[2,t], N[3,t]+N[4,t])
}

# Observation model
for (t in 1:n.occasions){
  C[t] ~ dpois(N[4,t])
}


Where C[t] = c(NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,8024,NA,NA,7334,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,7729,NA,NA,NA,6374,4796,NA,NA,8635)
.
Again, I apologize for what is likely a silly question. Ideally I would use a normal distribution to define my observation equation but my observed and estimated counts are quite different when I don't use the Poisson. Any advice or suggestions would be greatly appreciated!

Cheers,

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Node inconsistent with parent in Poisson observation model of count data
parts:
Hi Sarah,
The strategy I would suggest to debug this would be to create a model with nimbleModel, calculate, and look at individual nodes. For example, if model is the result of nimbleModel, you could look at:
model$calculate() # probably -Inf or NaN if something is not valid
model$calculate("C[21]")  # confirm a problem specifically for C[21]
model$C[21] # look at the value
model$N[4, 21] # Look at the value: is it valid as a Poisson parameter given the value of c[21]?
etc.
Given the temporal sequence of dbin, a first guess would be if N[4, 21] is 0 and C[21] is not 0.
If you are not providing inits for all of the N[,] values, then many of them might simply be NA. If you need values filled in, you could use model$simulate('N')
HTH. If you're still stuck, please see if you can send a fully reproducible example.
Perry
